checks.name: T039-F07 single-owned-lease enforcement in production code
checks.command_or_evidence: source inspection of GatewaySession::AcquireLease (src/xverse/xcom/src/tool_gateway.cpp ~1310), ReleaseLease ~1385, cleanup_locked ~676, and the public contract in src/xverse/xcom/include/xverse/xcom/tool_gateway.hpp ~515
checks.measured: AcquireLease now declines any acquisition while lease_held_ is true, returning LEASE_CONFLICT with diagnostic gw.lease.held and the retained original lease_id, incrementing requests_rejected_, and never calling the registry acquire. The request identity is computed into a local and assigned to lease_request_id_ only on LeaseStatus::Ok, so a declined acquisition cannot overwrite lease_key_, lease_request_id_, or lease_id_. ReleaseLease still requires the exact held lease_id and releases the original key; cleanup_locked releases or quarantines the original key on disconnect, cancellation, and shutdown. The method holds the session mutex, so the held-check and allocation are serialized. No other site mutates the lease members.

checks.measured: All four probe modes pass in both builds. two-leases: first acquisition svc.alpha state=1 LEASE_ACTIVE registry_active=1; the second acquisition svc.beta returns transport OK state=5 (LEASE_CONFLICT) with the ORIGINAL lease_id gw-lease-3 and registry_active=1 (no second active lease, no aliasing); after owner-watch cancellation terminal=1 lease_held=0 registry_active=0 registry_released=1. The R2 failure (two active leases and registry_active=1 after disconnect) no longer reproduces. cancel-queued, deadline-queued, and unread-shutdown also pass in both builds (cancel-queued terminal=1 with first durable outcome; deadline-queued second call DEADLINE_EXCEEDED with one emission; unread-shutdown terminal=1, socket removed, 1 ms normal and 10 ms under sanitizers). The two new F07 cases assert the complete contract against the authoritative fixture lease registry, not only gateway bookkeeping: RepeatedAcquireLeaseDeclinesSecondAllocation requires the second and repeated acquisitions to return LEASE_CONFLICT with the original lease_id, requires registry active == 1 throughout, requires QuerySession to report the retained lease, and requires owner cancellation to leave registry active == 0; RepeatedAcquireLeaseOriginalIdentityStillReleases requires the original identity to release the lease with registry active == 0 and released == 1. observations: The single-owned-lease boundary is enforced by declining a second allocation rather than by tracking a bounded owned set; an expanded multi-lease ownership model remains explicitly out of scope and would require its own design. Rejected acquisitions return LEASE_CONFLICT and preserve the original identity, which is the contract the R2 review required.

The successor record and the benchmark report limitations retain the historical clause that the admitted offline envelope cannot link the gRPC transport runtime (T032-GAP-01). This clause is now conservative rather than wrong in effect: it understates the successor capability, is scoped to the T036 benchmark's in-process owned-loopback workload and its accepted in-process sources, and the T032 component it names does retain that limitation. It is not an acceptance-supporting claim, so it is recorded here as an observation for a later refresh rather than as a blocking finding.

Watch ownership remains a logical lifecycle association keyed by an opaque identifier, not OS process authentication; clients must keep the identifier private. A running host action callback must still return before shutdown can complete. Durable lookup reconciles a committed immediate outcome; the absence of a scheduled intent remains explicitly uncertain and does not authorize a retry. These limits are carried into the maintained client guidance.

This review reproduced the R3 record's focused measures (524/524 normal, 524/524 sanitizer, the ten generated-client cases in both builds, 150 pytest tests plus 24 subtests, both report verifiers, and the requirements validator) and independently ran the immutable external closure probes; it did not rebuild the separate trusted integration (build/f8i) or validation (build/f8v) measures, rerun the inherited conformance replay, or regenerate the trace and benchmark reports from scratch.

The R2 review's identity checks and historical probe logs were treated as immutable inputs at their pinned hashes; the external probe file, the shared fixture, and the closure-gate script all match the admitted trusted-input digests, so the reproduced F07 result is attributable to this successor rather than to a substituted artifact.
limitations: This is a read-only internal review of the uncommitted T039 R3 successor; docs/engineering/xcom/t038/internal-review.json is the only artifact written, and no production code, test, evidence validator, host input, stage record, package record, or platform-main file was edited.

The trusted target-repository assembly and the integration, validation, static-analysis, and conformance measures are repeated by the trusted runner at the pinned candidate revision; this review verified the successor's focused evidence and did not substitute for that runner.

No OS-process authentication, arbitrary-callback preemption, exhaustive concurrency correctness, durability across every storage failure, or safe retry of an absent scheduled outcome is established. No ThreadSanitizer run, new generator replay, or production-performance claim is made.
External T039/T040 inspection, the separate successor review, and T041 explicit user acceptance remain open gates; this review neither accepts nor merges the candidate.
